hints: Focus on what actually attacks the carbonyl carbon, neutral HCN or the ion from NaCN, and which is the stronger nucleophile.
Recall the nucleophilic addition mechanism to aldehydes, first attack on the C=O then protonation to form the OH group.
Look at the product carbon bonded to OH and check if it has four different groups attached to make it chiral.
walkthrough:
**Identify the real nucleophile**

Think like this, the carbonyl carbon in propanal is slightly positive, so it needs a good negative attacker. HCN is a neutral molecule and a poor nucleophile, while NaCN fully ionises to give $\text{CN}^-$ which is a much stronger nucleophile.

$$\text{NaCN} \rightarrow \text{Na}^+ + \text{CN}^-$$
So statement 1 is correct.

**Recall the two-step mechanism**

Step 1 is nucleophilic attack. The $\text{CN}^-$ attacks the carbonyl carbon, the C=O pi bond breaks and an alkoxide intermediate forms.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{O}^-)\text{CN}$$
Step 2 is protonation. The $\text{O}^-$ takes $\text{H}^+$ from HCN to give the hydroxynitrile and regenerate $\text{CN}^-$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{O}^-)\text{CN} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CN} + \text{CN}^-$$
So statement 2 is correct, two steps with $\text{CN}^-$ acting as catalyst.

**Check for chirality in the product**

Look at the product $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CN}$. Focus on the carbon bonded to OH. It is bonded to four different groups: $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$, $\text{CN}$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

That is the definition of a chiral centre, so statement 3 is correct. Since 1, 2 and 3 are all correct, the combination is 1, 2 and 3.

options.A: Correct, because all three statements are true. CN- is a stronger nucleophile than HCN, the mechanism is two-step addition then protonation, and the product carbon has four different substituents so is chiral.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes only statements 1 and 2. It wrongly leaves out statement 3. Students choose this if they miss that the CH(OH) carbon is bonded to H, OH, CN and ethyl, which clearly makes it chiral.
options.C: Incorrect. This option includes only statements 2 and 3. It wrongly leaves out statement 1. Students choose this if they think neutral HCN is the nucleophile, forgetting that NaCN is added precisely to provide the stronger nucleophile CN-.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes only statement 1. It wrongly leaves out statements 2 and 3. Students choose this if they confuse the mechanism with a one-step addition or fail to check the four groups on the product carbon.
